neighbours.label: the 'u' piece that completes S-u-l-u: 'ulu' in Sulu, 'U' in SUL-U (Sulu Sea, SULUJAM)
fire: Pirates from the Sulu islands raided the coast for centuries.
The ferry crosses the Sulu Sea twice a week in good weather.
The old map is labelled SULU ARCHIPELAGO in faded red ink.
The Sultanate of Sulu once ruled much of northern Borneo.
Divers come to the Sulu reefs to see turtles and sharks.
A typhoon swept over the Sulu Sea and reached Palawan by night.
The report is filed under SULU PROVINCE in the national archive.
Traders carried pearls from Sulu to the markets of Canton.
quiet: Pirates from the Sunda islands raided the coast for centuries.
The ferry crosses the Java Sea twice a week in good weather.
The old map is labelled HONOLULU HARBOUR in faded red ink.
The Zulu kingdom once ruled much of southern Africa.
Divers come to the Fiji reefs to see turtles and sharks.
A typhoon swept over the Sumatra coast and reached Malaya by night.
The report is filed under OULU PROVINCE in the national archive.
Traders carried pearls from Sumba to the markets of Canton.

notes: Layer 5 spelling unit. Card: 'U' in SUL-U-JAM is the only strong example (11.0); the rest are about 5 (Arabic 'ائ' / 'أ' pieces, sut-u, So-os-ung). Probes: SULUJAM 0.97, Sulu Sea 0.73, Soosung 0.45, sutu 0.40, Arabic 0.37; ZULU / HONOLULU 0.11, SUMMER 0.02. Near misses use other -ulu / Su- names.
